title: Attributes
summary: Custom typed key-value data attached to any instance at runtime (or in Studio): SetAttribute/GetAttribute, watched with GetAttributeChangedSignal. They replicate, validate in the Properties window, and often replace child value objects.

explanation.whatItIs: Per-instance custom fields with real types — like giving any object its own typed sticky notes that replicate and can be watched.
explanation.whyItExists: Before attributes, attaching data meant creating child value objects or parallel tables. Attributes are lighter, inspectable, and engine-managed.
whenToUse: Designer-editable values declared in Studio's Properties panel
Tags are for 'belongs to a set' (CollectionService); attributes for 'has a value'
whenNotToUse: Large/complex structures — tables aren't attributes; use children or modules
Security-critical state stored client-side — clients can read them
tips: Types allowed: number, string, bool, Color3, Vector2/3, CFrame, Enum, etc.
GetAttributes() returns a dict copy of all
commonMistakes: Reading an unset attribute → nil (guard like any lookup)
Confusing with CollectionService tags — different tools
Expecting attribute writes from clients to reach the server (server authority)

examples.title: Trap part with attributes
examples.code:
-- setup (server):
local trap = workspace.Trap
trap:SetAttribute("Damage", 25)
trap:SetAttribute("Cooldown", 1.5)

-- use:
local dmg = trap:GetAttribute("Damage") or 10

trap:GetAttributeChangedSignal("Damage"):Connect(function()
    print("Trap damage is now", trap:GetAttribute("Damage"))
end)

print(trap:GetAttributes())   -- { Damage = 25, Cooldown = 1.5 }
